sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Cambridgeshire
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised Cambridgeshire scope to about 35,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £77 million.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original page described up to 45,000 premises.
Commercial-rollout expansion drove the redesign and does not itself show live service.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Suffolk
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised Suffolk scope to about 60,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £118.2 million.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 79,500 premises and £100.5 million.
Redesigned intervention scope is not equivalent to current orderable coverage.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - East and West Sussex
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised East and West Sussex scope to about 13,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £25.2 million.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 52,000 premises and £100 million.
Premises scope remains subject to detailed supplier planning and technical change.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised scope to about 6,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £24.4 million.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 34,000 premises and £58 million.
The redesign aims to avoid overlap and is not direct evidence of a live connection.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Leicestershire and Warwickshire
sources.lines: May 2026 redesign and original contract details
facts: The May 2026 redesign revised scope to about 36,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £76.4 million.
CityFibre is the named supplier.
The original contract described about 38,000 premises and £71 million.
Award and redesign metadata require delivered-premises evidence before parcel promotion.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - North Shropshire
facts: Freedom Fibre was originally awarded a contract for 12,000 premises.
The page states 2,500 premises had been completed and a further 1,000 were targeted before descope.
The remaining 8,500 premises were descoped from the Freedom Fibre contract.
In April 2026 BDUK added premises to an Openreach call-off contract covering other parts of Shropshire.
Completed, targeted, descoped and transferred premises must remain separate statuses.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
facts: Wildanet was awarded the contract.
The stated scope is about 16,800 hard-to-reach premises.
The stated contract value is £41.2 million.
The contract was signed in April 2024.
Awarded scope requires separate delivered and orderable-service verification.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Dorset and South Somerset
facts: Wessex Internet was awarded the contract.
The stated scope is about 21,400 hard-to-reach premises.
The stated contract value is £33.5 million.
The contract was signed in March 2024.
Construction preparation is distinct from service availability.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - New Forest
facts: Wessex Internet was awarded the contract.
The stated scope is about 10,500 hard-to-reach premises.
The stated contract value is nearly £14 million.
The contract was signed in March 2023.
Contract scope and nearby build do not establish service at an individual UPRN.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Derbyshire Peak District
facts: BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the Peak District contract.
BDUK stated it was arranging alternative supplier plans.
In April 2026 the area was added to an existing Openreach call-off contract.
A terminated contract cannot be treated as current delivery evidence.
Replacement procurement status remains distinct from built or orderable service.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - Lincolnshire and East Riding of Yorkshire
facts: Quickline was awarded the contract.
The stated scope is about 72,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The stated contract value is £118.9 million.
Multiple local authorities are identified as delivery partners.
Award data require built-premises and orderability evidence before exact promotion.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contract - West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean
facts: BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the original contract.
BDUK stated it was arranging alternative plans for affected premises.
In April 2026 West Herefordshire was added to an Openreach call-off contract.
Forest of Dean and West Herefordshire status must not be silently conflated.
Replacement contract coverage still requires exact delivered-premises evidence.
